summary.title: LLaDA2.0-Uni: Unifying Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Diffusion Large Language Model

setting_and_object.category: Architecture (unified multimodal discrete diffusion model / system)

details: Existing unified masked-diffusion multimodal models lag behind autoregressive unified models because their reconstruction-based VQ tokenizers lack semantics (hurting understanding) and over-compress images (hurting generation), and fully bidirectional attention is unreliable for text.
Alternative unified models use decoupled visual modules (ViT for understanding, VAE for generation), creating a modeling gap with divergent objectives.

LLaDA2.0-Uni: a unified discrete diffusion LLM in which both understanding and generation operate on the SAME fully-semantic discrete visual tokens, trained end-to-end under a single block-wise masked-diffusion (mask prediction) objective.

Three components: a SigLIP-VQ tokenizer producing semantic (not pixel-reconstructive) discrete image tokens, a 16B MoE dLLM backbone with an expanded vocabulary and block-wise attention, and a separate diffusion decoder that renders the generated semantic tokens back into high-fidelity images (also doing 2x super-resolution).

Efficiency mechanisms: SPRINT, a training-free inference accelerator combining modality-aware key-norm/confidence-based prefix KV pruning with confidence-thresholded non-uniform token unmasking; plus consistency distillation of the decoder to 8-step CFG-free sampling.

Backbone: LLaDA-2.0-mini, an MoE dLLM with 16B total parameters; vocabulary extended with the 16,384-entry SigLIP-VQ codebook (dim 2048) plus special tokens; new visual embeddings randomly initialized, language parts kept from pretraining.
Tokenizer: SigLIP2-g ViT encoder + vector quantizer (following X-Omni), dynamic resolution, quantized features aligned to a pretrained LLM.
Positioning: original 1D RoPE retained; explicit <height>/<width> size tokens (e.g. <imgsize_512>) prepended to flattened visual sequences for arbitrary resolution.
Diffusion decoder: built on Z-Image-Base (6B T2I), conditioned solely on (upsampled) semantic visual tokens with no text prompt.

Understanding: open-source captions plus curated OCR (PaddleOCR pseudo-labels refined by Qwen3-VL), grounding/counting (Objects365, RefCOCO, coords normalized to [0,1000]), knowledge/reasoning, and text-only data from Ling2.0/LLaDA2.0; ~60M SFT samples at 1:5 text-to-multimodal ratio with query and response filtering.
Generation: 200M+ web images filtered by resolution/compression, ArtiMuse aesthetics (>60) and DeQA-Score (>4.0) to 140M; captions from Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B that fuse informative original web text.
Editing: mix of X2Edit, OmniEdit, Pico-Banana, UniWorld, etc., plus synthesized pairs; VLM filtering of failed edits and instruction rewriting.

Interleaved: Koala36M videos filtered by duration/aesthetics/clarity/motion (~75% removed, 6M clips), frames every 5s giving 2-6 frame sequences; ~8M reasoning-augmented samples from Flux-6M, Zebra-CoT, Weave.

Three stages: S0 vision-language alignment (100B tokens, generation resolution 256->512), S1 multi-task pretraining (210B tokens, 512), S2 SFT (80B tokens, sequence length 8192->16384; decoder to 1024).
Objective: Block Diffusion (BDLM) masked-prediction loss; task-specific masking (mask only image tokens for generation, only text tokens for understanding).
SFT additions: mask-token reweighting with per-sample weight = 1/sqrt(#masked tokens) to counter length imbalance, plus complementary masking.
MoE: auxiliary-loss-free load balancing with RMS-normalized bias updates and routing gate outputs scaled by 2.5.

Decoder: flow matching in three phases (frozen-semantic warm-up, full-parameter multi-domain, high-fidelity refinement), then consistency distillation with an auxiliary projection layer and JVP/UCGM second-order approximation.
Infrastructure: offline VQ token pre-extraction, offline data packing into fixed-length sequences, dFactory/VeOmni distributed training.

Understanding: 21 benchmarks spanning general VQA (MMStar, MMBench, HallusionBench), reasoning (MMMU/-Pro, MathVista, MathVision), OCR/chart (ChartQA, DocVQA, OCRBench, CharXiv), plus CountBench and V*; baselines Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LLaDA-V, BAGEL, InternVL-U, Lumina-DiMOO, LLaDA-o.

Generation: GenEval, DPG-Bench, OneIG-EN, UniGenBench, CVTG-2K (text rendering), WISE-Bench (reasoning-informed); baselines FLUX.1[Dev], Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Seedream 3.0, Emu3, Janus-Pro, BAGEL, OmniGen2, HunyuanImage 3.0, NextFlow, MMaDA, Lumina-DiMOO, LLaDA-o.
Editing: ImgEdit-Bench, GEdit-Bench (EN/CN), MICo-Bench multi-reference; baselines FLUX.1 Kontext, Step1X-Edit, Qwen-Image-Edit, Z-Image-Edit, BAGEL, OmniGen2, InternVL-U.
New benchmark: InterGen, 150 interleaved-generation samples in three categories judged by Gemini-3 and Qwen3-VL on text coherence, text-image alignment, ID consistency; compared against Emu3.5.
Ablations: SPRINT settings (keep ratios r_text=1.0/r_img=0.8 vs full retention, global r=0.5; confidence threshold tau in {0.93, 0.95}) and distilled decoder analysis.

key_findings.finding: Using fully semantic discrete visual tokens lets a unified masked-diffusion model reach specialized VLM-level multimodal understanding, closing the gap left by reconstruction-based VQ tokenizers.
key_findings.evidence: Across 21 understanding benchmarks it beats diffusion-based unified models (MMStar 64.1 vs 58.0; MMMU 50.1 vs 44.9) and matches or slightly exceeds Qwen2.5-VL-7B on MMStar (64.1 vs 63.9) and CountBench (86.0 vs 84.9), including strong OCR/document results where Lumina-DiMOO struggles.

key_findings.finding: The same unified discrete-token model attains state-of-the-art text-to-image generation among unified models and is competitive with generation-only specialists.
key_findings.evidence: GenEval overall 0.89 with best Position score 0.90 across all evaluated models; DPG-Bench 87.76 (vs LLaDA-o 87.04, HunyuanImage 3.0 86.10) with top Entity 93.55 and Other 94.04; UniGenBench-EN 79.63 overall with leading Logic 63.99 and Layout 90.30; OneIG-EN 0.505 overall with best unified Alignment 0.882 and Reasoning 0.323, but weaker dense text rendering.

key_findings.finding: The architecture excels at multi-reference and instruction-based editing, where an architecturally similar discrete-diffusion baseline fails.
key_findings.evidence: MICo-Bench state-of-the-art 47.1 vs OmniGen2 33.8, Qwen-Image 35.9, and Lumina-DiMOO 23.3; ImgEdit overall 3.92 best among unified models (OmniGen2 3.44, InternVL-U 3.67); GEdit 6.61 EN / 6.66 CN with strong perceptual quality.

key_findings.finding: Reasoning before generation substantially improves world-knowledge-dependent image generation.
key_findings.evidence: WISE-Bench overall 0.68, first among unified models and on par with LongCat-Image, with an additional ~10% improvement when the reasoning mode is enabled.

key_findings.finding: SPRINT provides training-free inference acceleration for block-wise diffusion decoding with little quality loss.
key_findings.evidence: Combining modality-aware prefix KV pruning (r_text=1.0, r_img=0.8, global r=0.5) with confidence-threshold adaptive unmasking yields up to 1.6x speedup; the decoder is separately distilled to 8-step CFG-free sampling instead of 50-step CFG.
